reviews.text: 稍微提供一些购买建议。 简单来说这就是个粉丝向的IP作品，而且还是已经停服的氪金手游废物利用去掉内购做出来的，玩法基本就是猫咪大战争。 通过推关和解锁成就能获得相当多的抽卡道具，重复刷关卡可以获得装备技能升级材料等等，基本按照常见氪金手游那套模式去理解就行了，感觉卡关打不过有压力就回头刷刷材料升级强化一下，不用担心操作问题，提供了贴心的4倍速自动战斗，虽然AI非常无脑但靠数值碾压也可以做到基本无手操推关。 抽卡方面根据主线进度限制了一下卡池，这个我觉得没什么问题，毕竟再怎么说也不是一上来抽个最新ssr就能秒杀一切的氪金手游了，最开始就提供强过头的兵种恐怕会导致连基础的游戏体验都没了。刚开局只能抽到normal和rare稀有度的卡，虽然看起来磕碜但好歹基本都是只玩过街机就能认识的熟面孔，那些手游才出场的各路妖魔鬼怪大都在更高稀有度里，而且靠充足的抽卡资源可以轻易叠卡突破获得更大的面板优势，但又不会过于逆天所以实战中还是能看到一点敌我双方拉扯，这也是我觉得这游戏为数不多的玩法上的乐趣了。 顺便一提满突的卡不会再出现在卡池中，因此可以推测虽然抽卡资源的获取都是一次性的，但全通关后应该是可以全收集全满突的。

本作最初为免费手游版，后以defence为名登录steam（同样为免费版可以先体验一下，没有强制氪金内容）。此次以reloaded为名还是做了一些内容完善的，特别是剧情为全新。该系列玩法较为成熟，可为主系列之外一个不错的衍生系列。不过该系列宣传很少，导致知道的人不多，属于隐藏的佳作。对于白嫖且全成就前两作的人，此次第一时间入手本作也算是再次支持下snk，希望复活格斗游戏之外也能为本系列找到发展。

别人花8万块钱抽出来的小妹妹，我用风灵月影叮一下就获得了，可真是手手又游游啊…… 玩了一会儿，意外的发现他居然真的认真做了一下，手游版本中那些奇奇怪怪的二次元小姑娘都被囊括进去了，但是删掉了那些不同节日版本的角色，有了新的剧情，有中文，并且他还真的依据游戏难度进行了数据系统的重做，虽然还是一股子氪金手游的味儿，但就冲着他明明可以不冲厕所，但还是给马桶上雕了花这一点来说，令人感动的屎尿横流。 虽然我打了好评，但是我还是建议你别买。

太肝了，还没有自动重复刷图，这还不是主要的，要命的是材料竟然是靠打地图里隐藏攻击点救人获得（虽然很还原街机），但开自动那傻子AI根本不会自己去打，只能随缘，自己打就算了，5个队300个人，每人五个装备栏，每个装备栏里面要填6个材料......别说什么单玩一队，这游戏没有这个选项，强制你玩5个派系，冲练度，不然卡你主线......神经病啊，都不是手游了，随意点不好吗？抽卡也不能10连，一个一个的去点，成就那边也是一个一个的点，我感觉我鼠标寿命在下降。至于平衡就不说了，反正单机无所谓，但是真的肝，操作还繁琐，挂机不存在的，这辈子都不可能挂机的。 也不知道后续会不会改，还没有入手的最好先别买，不然2个小时过去，后悔也莫得用。

好评嘛？好评！给谁的？给合金弹头的。 我知道虚幻4引擎是能做2D游戏的，但是我完全没想到$BK会把曾经关服的手游MSA拿出来用虚幻4炒了一波冷饭我是没想到的，任天堂直面会一结束各大主机加PC（steam）纷纷上架然后以71.36大洋的价格把这份冷饭拿出来了。狠啊，真狠啊！然后我就和一些朋友们在看到游戏上架后就入手了这份冷饭，然后我吃了好几天的土。。。。（啪~！） 不过也不是一点新的东西都没有，全新的开场界面，从原来的在线模式换成了单机离线模式，存档从存在服务器种变成了存在本地。虽然提供了在线对战的玩法，但是不像以前手机的在线版本那样经过服务器，而是P2P联机，以至于刚发售那阵子甚至有传闻说盗版也可以直接进行在线对战。6啊，很6啊！ 游戏也把MSA时期一些角色的设定图放进来了，当然也不是全部。在包含了MS1-2/X-3-4-5-6-7/XX-3D-DEFENCE和ATTACK的所有BGM的同时，$BK也专门为这个冷饭制作了三首新BGM。单位并不全但是有一个全新的单位“莫斯托洛”，然而据说也是MSA关服时期就被解包出来过的单位，属于是完全因为这次冷饭重新得到了登场机会。给的设定也是不少合金弹头玩家都很喜欢的BOSS火星之根。。的娘化版（剧情设定是和一个死去的日本女孩灵魂融合了）增加了一些新的机制以及主线关卡剧情。整体的感觉你不能说不好但是给人的感觉又很廉价，很多设计完全就是为了拖时长而设计，MSA设计的一部分UI交互甚至比现在的冷饭还要方便。因为变成了单机，没有了体力系统，所以游戏也就没有了扫荡功能，玩家刷材料要经过漫长的过程。以至于现在大部分人都会选择使用变速软件加速通关过程，甚至强化交互也是极其繁琐，现在全球范围内无论是手游还是各大游戏都知道简化强化流程，我不信$BK不懂，毕竟MSA后期他们就做到了。就说明$BK本身就是在故意卡玩家时长。 同时阵营性能参差不齐，强的真强，刮的真刮。然后单位获取依旧要抽卡，只是池子可以抽空。有人表示可以试图修改MSP和勋章。然而我给你的答复就是修改毫无意义，你拿到了强力单位不代表你就赢了，你还要经历极其漫长的养成过程。只是拿到就想着去打高难关卡最终只能让敌人啪啪扇自己嘴巴子，通过加大游戏难度来延长游戏时长，只能说不愧是$BK。 在线对战本是展现玩家对自己配置的一个实力展现，也是这个游戏的特色。但是因为游戏现在对战方式从服务器变成了俩台主机之间P2P交互。以至于作弊开挂比以前成本还低，曾经MSA时期想要举报作弊玩家，通常都会选择在周一到周五时像$BK发举报邮件来进行封禁作弊玩家，但是现在因为是俩台电脑或者主机直接交互，数据不走服务器。你就算发邮件给$BK，估计也不会有什么封禁答复。对于$BK来说，反正无论输赢你都能拿到勋章，大不了你可以和你一起买这游戏的好友一起1v1啊~（bushi）。而且游戏开始之前就有起名字这么一说，你记名字，那人家只要把存档删了再重起个名字新建存档就完事了。 游戏本身只存在反修改加密但是一点反作弊都没有。我说实在的，$BK你们要是真做不到反作弊，那咱们就别搞在线对战好不好呢？同时还有那么多单位包括黄金单位以及节日，特务单位没出。是不是打算搞DLC？讲真的，我很希望我花的这71.36大洋，是给合金弹头正统续作的奶粉钱，而不是让你们搁那天天发动态搁那自嗨的医疗费。能买这游戏的真的可能，除了真爱粉，就是那些以前接触过合金弹头的情怀玩家，你这游戏里面大部分的种种难崩设定对于真爱粉可能还会给予包容，但是路人或者那些情怀玩家人家早就全球网络论坛求修改了。 你问我这游戏适不适合入坑？你要是有钱，曾经还玩过MSA，对MSA有着特殊的执念。或许这游戏适合你。但是路人的话，还是快跑吧。各种意义上的快跑。 （顺带一提，真不考虑搞个创意工坊？[dog]）

小时候某个周末和我妈逛商场我照例到负一层的街机厅里玩合金弹头，二十块钱的游戏币打了半个小时，直到我妈购完物带着热乎的烤鸡来找我，坐在我旁边的空位等着我打完手头剩下的币，还记得那关的最后是在打丧尸，眼看快结束了让我妈拿手机拍里面的像素小人然后回家画下来。 后来搬家距离那个商场很远，几乎再没去过了。 那一天的记忆里有热腾腾的烤鸡，坐在旁边的妈妈，手机里角度没对好拍的有点模糊的像素小人，他们好像被合金弹头这个游戏串了起来，形成了一段独特的回忆，又被这些意象赋予了别样的情感，至今难忘，以至每每看到合金弹头这段记忆都要再浮现一次，不禁潸然泪下。

系列新作，不过据说最初发售在手机上，我基本不碰手游，所以不太了解。 ​这其实是个互推塔防类型，角色众多，大部分关卡靠刷等级和装备就能过。但是Another Story里面个别的最高难度还是需要合适的角色搭配加上手动才能通过，尤其想要获得S评价更是如此，我是参考了下B站的视频顺利达成的。 虽然本质比较肝，不过由于可以设置自动战斗，所以刷的部分可以同时忙别的事情，基本不耗费精力。 因为不包括AS的最高难度关卡，所以​全成就倒是不难，角色装备满级的话，开自动就行，所以早就达成了，但是为了单机部分的完美，还是继续完善了下。网络部分就算了，联机都找不到人，我也对这种类型的对战兴趣不大，就放弃了。 ​这是我的第一个Steam游戏，第二个Steam软件，支持下《合金弹头》系列，就当做给SNK提供奶粉钱了。 游戏内置的目标，除了网站的3个，全都达成了。 ​包括全故事通常和精英的双模式的全难度S评价、全AS关卡的全难度S评价、全终极任务的全难度S评价。 ​游戏内置的目标以外，全角色的【POWER UP】以外的全状态满。而【POWER UP】的部分，只有终极任务获得的5个终极兵器以及一些常用主力是满的，道具实在太难刷了。 ​游戏基本算是圆满，以后看心情慢慢再刷一下【POWER UP】吧。

Before I spiel, a warning to prospective buyers: This game hasn't been updated since November of '24. And, in light of total radio-silence from SNK, it would seem as if MSA: Reloaded has been abandoned indefinitely for the foreseeable future. Expect no future updates. Online match-making functionality seemingly still works, but good luck finding an opponent. With that out of the way, enjoy my tirade while I highlight what I despise about this game, and where I think it succeeds. To keep it brief, I'ma simmer down my review to three talking points. 1: For those who don't know, MSA: Reloaded is a remake of a mobile game that went down shortly before Reloaded's release. MSA, should memory serve, was up since 2016 unto 2024, and in that time accrued a loyal fanbase, a myriad of gamemodes, and a truly incredible roaster spanning thousands of characters, including unique character variants. Even if we were to remove redundant gamemodes and character variants, Reloaded is simply missing many game modes and dozens, if not hundreds of unique characters from the original. That's really the crux of the issue: The game's simply missing alot of content from the original with very little new stuff to show for it, and it doesn't look like any of that old stuff will ever be readded. So know, this version of MSA is an extremely watered-down version of what once was. 2: The core-gameplay loop is appealing and entertaining and the battle system is good. But flaws in the game's structure enfeebles it. In MSA, the game was about gambling for waifus foremost, and wasn't too difficult outside of multiplayer and event content. Strategy often gave way for sheer power, yet held some small measure of significance and incurred a benefit for whoever cared enough to engage with it. And besides for limited event characters, basically every unit was available to you via the two gacha pools at all times. So even if you never got the person you wanted, you at least always had the chance to get anyone on the list, regardless of level or progression. In Reloaded, that dynamic has changed in the hopes of giving the player a more curated experience. Units are further segregated into different "Gacha tiers", and certain tiers are blocked off from you until you reach certain points in the campaign. Meaning that at any point in the campaign, there's only a very limited amount of units you'll have access too, and will be relative in strength to what the enemy has... Kinda. That isn't innately bad, linear progression has it's place. But keep that in mind. The game takes a more tactical approach as well - leaning heavier on strategy than the original, and is a good deal more difficult. Normally, I could get behind this, but the game's gacha system doesn't help facilitate that shift in focus, as since you're gambling for units (even though medals are now free), certain strats and unit synergies could be blocked off from you entirely if you're particularly unlucky. That doesn't pair well at all with the fact that the AI cheats - being able to spam units far faster than you can, can deploy units at the start of the game before you even generate your first point of AP, and occasionally uses more powerful units you don't have access too at that time, leading to an artificial spike in difficulty at multiple points in the campaign that you quite literally CANNOT surpass outside of grinding for levels so you can upgrade your units, which is (spoilers:) slower than molasses dripping of a spoon. This, to me, at least, is best displayed in level 8-1; The start of the Mexican missions. In this level, you're immediately swarmed by a legion of angry, tanky swordsmen, a tanky guy who can summon structures that produce more of said swordsmen, artillery that can sit behind them and strike you with with impunity, and a *whole lot* of them, and a scantily-clad ninja-waifu who's both far more durable than anything you can get (yes, even moreso than double-reinforced steelclad tanks), and is the human equivalent of a nuclear bomb. There's really no strategy you can employ to succeed. You just don't have the units - no matter how lucky you've been - or the time to get enough AP production to make it happen before you're swarmed and your units are rendered into burger. The only thing you CAN do is grind for literal hours to get 5-10 levels ahead of your foes to make up the deficit in stats and great difference in deployment speed. Which, as you can imagine, is annoying and tiresome, and not indicative of good design. 3: Reliance on "Another Story." (The least offensive of my three main issues, but still a pain). For those who don't know... Another story is an alternative gamemode that basically let's you play through poorly-written sidestories set within the MSA universe. In MSA, this was just fun, alternative side-content. In Reloaded, it's mandatory, at least early on, because you can't do the fifth set of missions without completing the first chapter in the PA story, if not in all of the five stories available to you. Worse yet, the game uses it as a means to force you to grind, because in Another story, you're forced to use units from the respective faction of whichever story you're playing through. For the PA, this mainly consists of weak, squishy guys with small arms, because that's really all you can get for them at this state, bar a couple of relatively weak vehicles. The problem here is that, because the boss for this chapter is a giant alien mothership suspended in the aether, only a handful of units (like, three so far as I know) can actually aim up high enough to target it, be it with their normal attack or their special. Naturally, you can't output enough damage to destroy a mothership with only a small number of units before it annihilates you, assuming you even have the few units that can damage it to begin with. Meaning, you have to gamble until you can get those units and then grind until you can make them strong enough to take the mothership down on their own, which - trust me - will take you a *reaaal* long time, regardless if you get lucky with your gacha rolls. TL;DR - game's a shell of what once was, and it ain't getting better than this, it would seem. If you love strategy and don't mind grindin' a bunch, are a fan of the Metal Slug franchise, or a former MSA player looking to relive your experience with the game, even in a watered-down state, this game is for you. Otherwise, stay far, far away.

[h3]As a Metal Slug Attack OG player who stopped playing almost three years ago cuz got shut down, after many hours of gameplay, I’m here to give my honest and realistic review.[/h3] First, comparing this version to the original, there are quite a few differences, some good, some bad. In terms of balance, the game seems much more even than the OG. Back in the original, simply obtaining a new unit and upgrading it to the max could let you win many battles against players with older units. In other words, there was a [b]"meta"[/b] revolving around the newest units: every time a new unit was released, the older ones became less effective. Now, speaking of units, this version of Metal Slug Attack is severely lacking in content i mean [b]A LOT[/b]. Many units, items, modes, and cranks are missing. From my perspective, this makes the game feel boring, because once you unlock all the available units [i](which isn’t difficult at all)[/i], there’s nothing left to do except replay levels. This, in turn, negatively impacts the player base: [b]online is completely empty.[/b] Regarding the current state of this so-called [b]"reloaded"[/b] version, it hasn’t received any updates in a long time, not even announcements. I want to send a message to the developers: If you’re going to revive a game, at least do it properly. This is a game that was widely loved, and its closure disappointed many fans. Remaking it wasn’t a bad idea, it gave hope and excitement to players. However, ceasing updates and not adding content is poor practice, especially considering that this version costs approximately [b]$9[/b], while the original was [b]FREE[/b]. [h3]So, do I recommend this game? Not at the moment. Right now, there’s very little purpose in spending time on it: there are no extra ops, no new cranks, no new content to spend your earnings on, and the online experience is nearly nonexistent.[/h3]

I didn't play the original, but I gotta say this was enjoyable for the first 15 hours. The pixel-art is amazing, and the different units are very cool and unique. I especially like the carnivorous plant that duplicates itself when using its special ability. My main problem lies with how economy is handled in a round. When you haven't upgraded your income much in the upgrades menu, the game has a much slower pace where you get to time your units' special abilities. As you get further and have a much faster income, the game instead forces you to spam units senselessly. In a game where the combat is so simple, you need the player's choices to matter and feel impactful. I rarely got that feeling after those first 15 hours, as all I could do is click deploy on all units I could afford without thinking. Overall, the game is still good enough to buy at a discount (like 60% or more) considering the staggering amount of attention to detail in the visuals.
